findings.finding: Variable-order Markov models, Prediction Suffix Trees, CTW and PPM are established sequence predictors that condition on recent suffix/history; immediate-predecessor-conditioned prediction is therefore ordinary prior art.
sources: Begleiter, El-Yaniv & Yona, On Prediction Using Variable Order Markov Models, JAIR 22 (2004), DOI 10.1613/JAIR.1491
Pereira, Singer & Tishby, Beyond Word N-Grams (1996), prediction suffix trees

findings.finding: Computational-mechanics causal states group histories by identical future conditional distributions and provide minimal predictively sufficient state; this is a sharper baseline than raw history sensitivity and has been applied directly to spike trains.
sources: Crutchfield & Shalizi, Phys. Rev. E 59, 275 (1999), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevE.59.275
The Computational Structure of Spike Trains, PMC (2010)

findings.finding: Predictive State Representations and belief-state methods make history-conditioned prediction under observation aliasing foundational; contemporary NeurIPS 2025 work continues to learn compact predictive belief representations under partial observability.
sources: Littman, Sutton & Singh, Predictive Representations of State, NeurIPS 2001
Kuo et al., Predictive Coding Enhances Meta-RL To Achieve Interpretable Bayes-Optimal Belief Representation Under Partial Observability, NeurIPS 2025
